about: Fortnite build pieces on Fortnite's grid (a tile is 5.12 m square, a storey 3.84 m tall). The DLL draws the Fortnite mesh and owns their collision: the Fortnite movement controller, camera and your bullets/rockets/pickaxe treat each piece as an oriented box. Pieces are stored in block-local coordinates with their map tile, so Havok re-basing never moves them. Enemy collision (spawning an Elden Ring asset) waits for a way to remove spawned assets: fromsoftware-rs has spawn but no despawn, and a destroyed wall must not leave collision behind.

columns.name: display name
columns.pitch_deg: tilt of the collision box (ramp: atan(3.84/5.12) = 36.87)
columns.pivot: placement rule: wall_edge | floor_cell | ramp_cell | cone_cell
columns.collision_asset: Elden Ring asset spawned so enemies collide with it, or none (0.1: none, see about)
columns.collision_base_size_m: [x,y,z] native size of that asset, for scaling ([0,0,0] when none)

_unverified_note: Ramp collision is a 6.4 m slab (the slope length of a 5.12 x 3.84 cell) tilted 36.87 degrees. The cone's collision is a 1.92 m tall box over its cell (a pyramid in Fortnite).
